dependencies.reason: extends its run function, start hooks, stores and schema steps, logger and scrubber, configuration loader and parleyd backup
the request id a log line must carry and the access-log line are created by its middleware

tasks.title: Refuse to serve without git 2.38 or later
steps: Add the behaviours of the version check to internal/gitrepo/version_test.go and internal/hub/gitcheck_test.go and confirm they fail; the tests place a script named git first on the PATH of the hub's environment lookup
Add version parsing to internal/gitrepo: read the two numbers after 'git version ', keep the text up to the first space, ignore the rest, and compare on major and minor only

Add the check itself: resolve git through a path lookup it is given, run git --version with a time limit it is given, kill the process when the limit passes, and return one of the four error texts of the PRD's table (not found, too old, cannot read, failed)

Register the check in the hub's composition as the start hook named git-version, ahead of every other start hook, with a limit of 10 seconds and the PATH of the hub's environment lookup; on success log one info line 'git version checked' with git_version
Confirm that the runs that end before the start hooks (--help, a usage error, backup, the bootstrap runs) still succeed on a PATH without git, changing nothing in them
Add the end-to-end test of the old-git start followed by the good start to test/e2e/operations_test.go
done_when: `go test ./internal/gitrepo/... ./internal/hub/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1` passes on a host with git 2.38 or later

tasks.title: Make every log line parseable, attributable and free of credentials
steps: Add the behaviours to internal/hub/logging_test.go, internal/server/headers_test.go and test/e2e/logging_test.go and confirm they fail
Write time in UTC ending in Z and the level as TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR, the trace level included; keep one line of output per logged line
Add request_id to every line logged with a context that carries the request id of package 02's middleware, and to no other line

Scrub attribute values of every type: render errors as their message, walk groups, lists and maps, render byte slices and text-rendered values, and pass each resulting string through the scrubber; leave numbers, booleans and durations as they are

Rely on package 02 for the access-log line's path member: its REQ-8.5 writes path as the URL path without the query string in internal/server/accesslog.go, so edit nothing in that file; the table in internal/server/headers_test.go only confirms the point for this package's log audit
Drop a line whose write to stderr fails, without returning the failure to the code that logged and without stopping the process
Add the log audit to test/e2e/logging_test.go: a hub at level trace, five requests carrying marker secrets, and the three assertions over the whole of stderr

tasks.title: Record a release's data and open every recorded release
steps: Add the behaviours to test/upgrade/compat_test.go, test/upgrade/record/record_test.go and test/upgrade/upgrade_test.go and confirm they fail
Add a read-only listing of a store's applied schema steps, in order of application, and of the registered steps of each store, to internal/store
Add the compatibility rule to test/upgrade: every recorded name registered, same relative order, the first offending step named with 'not registered' or 'out of order'

Add the recorder as a run function that takes its arguments, an output directory, stdout and stderr and returns the exit status: validate the name, refuse an existing archive, bootstrap and serve a hub in a temporary directory, create fixture.git with one commit on main under the workspace root, stop the hub, write the manifest and the .tar.gz, remove the temporary directory
Add test/upgrade/record/main.go, which calls the run function with the output directory test/upgrade/testdata
Record the first archive with `go run ./test/upgrade/record baseline` and add test/upgrade/testdata/baseline.tar.gz to the repository

Add the upgrade test: for every archive, apply the compatibility rule, start the hub on the unpacked data, and assert readiness, the applied steps, the admin token hash and the repository; start it a second time and assert that nothing was applied; fail when testdata holds no archive
done_when: running the recorder a second time with the name baseline exits 1 and leaves the archive unchanged

tasks.title: Prove that a backup taken under load restores to a hub that starts cleanly
steps: Add a load helper to test/e2e: four writers committing transactions of 10 rows to a table of the transactional store, one writer on the analytical store, and two git clients each pushing commit after commit to one bare repository under the workspace root; it records every error it sees and the commits pushed before a given moment
Add a restore helper to test/e2e that copies a snapshot's transactional store, analytics.db and workspace directory into the data directory of a new working directory and writes its config.toml

Add the restore test of an idle hub's snapshot: the restored hub applies no step, runs a registered start hook once before it listens, keeps the admin token hash, commits a transaction and accepts a push, and the snapshot's files are unchanged

Add the test under load, repeated for three backups of one running hub: no writer and no push fails, the restored hub is ready, both stores pass PRAGMA integrity_check, the load table's row count is a multiple of 10, and each repository passes git fsck with a head that is the source's head or an ancestor of it and a descendant of what was pushed before the backup
Where a test fails, correct the cause in the snapshot code of internal/store or internal/hub (the order of copying, a file copied while it changes) and not the test
done_when: `go test ./test/e2e/... -run Restore -count=5` passes five times in a row

tasks.title: Build the hub container image
steps: Add the engine lookup of the image tests to test/image and its table test: skip unless PARLEY_IMAGE_TESTS is 1, use PARLEY_CONTAINER_ENGINE or docker, fail naming a command that is not on the PATH
Add the hub image tests to test/image/hub_test.go; they build the image once per run with the build arguments VERSION, COMMIT and BUILD_TIME and remove the containers and the volume they create

Write containers/hub/Dockerfile with the repository root as its context: a build stage that builds parleyd and parley without cgo and with the three build values set through the linker flags of internal/buildinfo, and a final stage on a base whose packaged git is 2.38 or later

In the final stage: both binaries in /usr/local/bin, user and group id 10001, XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/var/lib/parley/config, XDG_DATA_HOME=/var/lib/parley/data, the directory /var/lib/parley owned by 10001, declared as a volume and used as working directory, port 8080 declared, the entry point parleyd in exec form and no default arguments
Add a .dockerignore at the repository root that keeps .git, .specs and test data out of the build context

Run the image tests with PARLEY_IMAGE_TESTS=1 on a host with a container engine and confirm they pass; confirm that without the variable `go test ./test/image/...` passes with every image test skipped
done_when: `PARLEY_IMAGE_TESTS=1 go test ./test/image/... -run Hub -count=1` passes where a container engine is installed

tasks.title: Build the reference sandbox image and the image contract check
steps: Add the contract check to test/image as a function that takes the engine and an image reference, runs git init, a commit and git rev-parse HEAD in a container of that image as its default user, and returns an error naming the image and git when one of them fails

Add the sandbox image tests to test/image/sandbox_test.go: the contract check against the reference image, against an image without git that the test builds, and against PARLEY_SANDBOX_IMAGE when that is set; the contents of the reference image; the command passing through unchanged as user 1000

Write containers/sandbox/Dockerfile: the same build stage for the parley CLI, and a final stage with git 2.38 or later, /bin/sh, the base image's CA certificates, parley in /usr/local/bin, a user with id 1000 and a writable home directory, no entry point, and no parleyd and no agent
Run the tests with PARLEY_IMAGE_TESTS=1 and confirm they pass
done_when: `PARLEY_IMAGE_TESTS=1 go test ./test/image/... -run Sandbox -count=1` passes where a container engine is installed

tasks.title: Ship Kubernetes manifests that run one hub on a persistent volume
steps: Add gopkg.in/yaml.v3 to go.mod and add deploy/kubernetes/manifests_test.go with the behaviours of the four manifest criteria; confirm they fail

Write configmap.yaml with a config.toml that sets [server] bind 0.0.0.0, port 8080 and an external_url, [logging] level info, and one [[oauth.providers]] table named github whose client_secret is ${GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET}
Write secret.example.yaml (Secret parley-secrets, stringData with GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET set to replace-me) and pvc.yaml (parley-data, ReadWriteOnce, 20Gi, no storage class)

Write deployment.yaml: one replica, strategy Recreate, one container of the parley-hub image with no command and no args, envFrom the secret, the claim mounted at /var/lib/parley, the ConfigMap's config.toml mounted by subPath at /var/lib/parley/config/config.toml, liveness on /healthz and readiness on /readyz at port 8080, runAsUser 10001, runAsNonRoot, fsGroup 10001, terminationGracePeriodSeconds 40
Write service.yaml: ClusterIP, port 8080 to the container's port, selecting the Deployment's pods
Load the ConfigMap's config.toml through the configuration loader of internal/config in the test, with the example Secret's keys as environment and with an empty environment

tasks.title: Run performance scenarios against a hub and report their verdicts
steps: Add the behaviours to test/perf/config_test.go, test/perf/stats_test.go and test/perf/run_test.go, with a stub hub built on net/http/httptest in test/perf/stub_test.go; confirm they fail

Add the configuration from an environment lookup: skip without PARLEY_PERF_URL, an error naming a missing PARLEY_PERF_TOKEN or PARLEY_PERF_WORKSPACE, the workspace list split on commas and trimmed, the capacity flag, the sandbox profile, the report path with its default in the system's temporary directory, and the scenario deadline and event wait as fields tests can shorten
Add the nearest-rank p95 and the verdict of a measurement against a target with the comparisons lt, le and ge

Add the scenario type (name, target, the variables it needs, its deadline, its body) and the registry that holds the fourteen names in the PRD's order with their targets; a scenario whose body is not yet written reports error with no measurement

Add the run: read GET /version within 10 seconds or fail naming the URL, pick a run id of 12 hexadecimal characters, run each scenario under its deadline, mark the ones whose variable is unset as skipped naming the variable, turn a failing request into status error with method, path, status and error_type, and always go on to the next scenario

Add the HTTP client of the harness on net/http: the bearer token on every request, durations measured from sending to the end of the response, hub text in details cut to 200 bytes and the token never copied into a detail or an error
Add the report: the JSON document of the PRD written to the report path, the same results logged as a table, and an error naming the path when it cannot be written
Add TestPerformanceTargets, which skips, fails or passes as the configuration and the run say and never fails for a missed, skipped or error result
Add the smoke test against a real in-process hub to test/perf/run_test.go
done_when: `go test ./test/perf/... -count=1` passes with no PARLEY_PERF variable set, and reports TestPerformanceTargets as skipped

tasks.title: Measure the latency and throughput targets
steps: Add the behaviours to test/perf/scenarios_test.go and extend the stub hub with the fork, source control, change, land, event and sandbox exec routes; confirm they fail. Take the request and response shapes of each route from the PRD section that owns it (docs/prd/04, 06, 07, 08, 13 and 14)
Add the set-up every scenario shares: a target branch perf/<run id> in the first workspace, never the default branch, and the record of every fork, sandbox and stream a scenario creates

Add the clean-up that runs when a scenario ends in any verdict: delete its forks and sandboxes, close its streams, and list each clean-up request answered with 400 or more in cleanup_errors with its method, path and status
Add fork_create, file_read, commit_create and sandbox_exec as request-duration scenarios with 50, 200, 50 and 50 samples; sandbox_exec is skipped without a sandbox profile

Add land (20 changes of 20 commits, one at a time, from the land request to the success of the land attempt), land_throughput (120 changes, at most 8 land requests in flight, landed times 60 over the seconds elapsed) and land_concurrency (16 land requests at once, counting the attempts that did not end in success as the measurement, not as request errors)
Add mergeability: 100 open changes, one more change landed to move the target, polling no faster than once per second until none reports unknown

Add event_latency: one subscriber on GET /events, 50 commits, the largest time from response to event, 0 for an event that came first, and error for an event that has not come after the event wait (10 seconds)
done_when: `go test ./test/perf/... -count=1` passes against the stub hub

tasks.title: Measure the capacity and sandbox targets
steps: Add the behaviours to test/perf/scenarios_test.go and extend the stub hub with limits on forks, changes, streams and sandboxes; confirm they fail

Add the capacity loop: create until the target count is reached or the hub refuses, report the count that existed at once, keep the refusal's error_type as the detail, and give the scenario the 60-minute deadline

Add active_forks over every listed workspace (moving on when one refuses), open_changes in the first workspace, event_streams on GET /events and sandboxes_running, each run only with PARLEY_PERF_CAPACITY=1, the last also only with a sandbox profile

Add sandbox_ready: 5 sandboxes of the configured profile one after the other, the largest time from the create response to the first read showing ready, and error with the state_reason when one reaches failed
Register the created forks, changes, streams and sandboxes with the clean-up of the latency task, so that a capacity scenario leaves nothing behind
done_when: `go test ./test/perf/... -count=1` passes against the stub hub
